Frank Wise School is an outstanding and inspirational community special school for pupils between the ages of 2 and 19 serving the area around Banbury. Recognised in 2024 by OfSTED as being a school where, “Adults offer an irresistible invitation to join in with learning, songs and joyful play.”, Frank Wise is characterised by a strong belief in highly individualised and inclusive provision. As such we group our pupils solely by age and are committed to providing weekly access to mainstream learning opportunities for all of our pupils. You can find out a bit more about the school in this introductory video.

Have Your Say on the Future of SEND in Oxfordshire
Have Your Say on the Future of SEND in Oxfordshire
The Oxfordshire Local Area Partnership is asking children, young people, parent carers and professionals to share their views on the draft Oxfordshire SEND Strategy 2026–2029 before it is finalised.
As part of the consultation, Oxfordshire Parent Carers Forum (OxPCF) is hosting two interactive webinars with the Oxfordshire Local Area Partnership.
The Future of SEND in Oxfordshire – Strategy & Reform
Find out about the draft Oxfordshire SEND Strategy, the emerging local SEND Reform Plan for delivering the national SEND reforms, and what these developments could mean for children, young people and families in Oxfordshire. You’ll also have the opportunity to ask questions directly to Local Area Partnership leads and take part in live polls.
Tuesday 7 July | 7.00–9.00pm Thursday 9 July | 12.00–2.00pm
Both webinars cover the same content, so you only need to attend one. If you’re unable to join us live, both sessions will be recorded and shared on the OxPCF website shortly afterwards.
You can also read the draft strategy and complete the consultation survey before 3 August 2026.
Find everything you need, including the draft strategy, consultation survey and webinar booking links:
https://www.oxpcf.org.uk/post/have-your-say-oxfordshire-s-draft-send-strategy

Families
School Day
The school day at Frank Wise begins at 9:00 am and runs through until 3:30 pm, providing a total of 32.5 hours per week, unless you are not yet of statutory school age, in which case the day is split into two half day sessions.
These run from: 9:00 am until 12:00 pm or: 12:35 pm until 3:35 pm
Children may arrive from 9.00 am onwards as staff are employed to supervise them. However, parents and transport operators are reminded that teachers do need time in the morning to prepare for the school day so you are asked to respect this by kindly not bringing pupils into the building before 9.00 am. We also request that you do not arrive in the school building to collect your child before 3:30.
For the Assessment Nursery, children can arrive from 9:00 am or 12:35 pm depending on whether they are attending for the morning or afternoon session.
The children can bring in packed lunches, or arrange to have a school dinner. We are able to cater for all dietary needs and can support those children who experience feeding difficulties with advice from the Speech and Language Therapy service.
While most children are transported to and from school, we are very happy to support parents and carers who would prefer that their child walks to school, cycles or uses public transport. For more information, please watch this introductory video or contact the school on 01295 263520.
If you should require further information then please contact the school on – 01295 263520
Play and Leisure
The school is very fortunate to have an Out of School Liaison Officer (OSLO) to assist in organising supported activities and play beyond the school, including funding and transportation to help every child to participate who would like to. In the past these have include DJ-ing courses, football coaching and Cubs / Scouts to name but a few.
If you would like some support with regard to helping your child to join in with play activities after school, weekends or during the school holidays then please contact the school on 01295 263520 or 07545 934951.

Residential Trips Programme
Frank Wise School recognises the valuable contribution that a wide range of additional activities, including day and residential trips, can make toward our pupils’ personal and social education. Feedback from our alumni families suggests that residential trips in particular play a crucial role in preparing young people for life beyond school.
We carefully increase the length of time that pupils spend on their residential trips as they progress through school, in order to maximise their success.
Residential Trips lengths: 6th Family Group – 2 nights 7th Family Group – 2 nights 8th Family Group – 3 nights 9th Family Group – 3 nights 10th Family Group – 3 or 4 nights Griffiths Centre – 3 or 4 nights
These trips are very carefully planned, and every effort is made to ensure that your child is both safe and well looked after. Just as at school, all the activities we undertake will be tailored to suit each individual child.

The Governors
Our Governing Body
The Governing Body at Frank Wise school works voluntarily for the good of the school and is responsible for overseeing all strategic matters relating to school life. The Governors are responsible for deciding and agreeing school policies and for ensuring that the school is run effectively so that it is able to meet its aims.
The Governors never lose sight of the fact that every decision they make ultimately affects the children and young adults who attend Frank Wise school.
The Governors have three sub committees; Personnel, Resources and Standards; they meet at least once a term to discuss curriculum, policy, finance, buildings, appointments, marketing, school improvements and very importantly, safety, health and well-being. These committees report to the full Governing body with recommendations.

The Griffiths Centre
About The Griffiths Centre
At Frank Wise School we believe that one of the central aims of the educational opportunities we deliver is to enable the children who arrive at the school to leave as young adults who are as independent as possible.
To help achieve this it is essential to recognise that irrespective of the pupil’s level of ability, the provision available throughout the school as they become older needs to reflect their changing age. This is achieved in a number of ways, such as ensuring that the work provided is age appropriate in terms of both the learning contexts and the resources used, that social areas are designed to reflect changing interests and social dynamics and that the curriculum provided adapts to the changes in emphasis and priority.
Within all Key Stages the curriculum is designed to reflect the priorities of specific age groups, whilst maintaining a core provision (see Frank Wise School Curriculum Framework) and the curriculum for the Griffiths Centre at Frank Wise School is no exception. As children become young adults and make the significant step from a Pre-16 to a Post-16 model of education our curriculum is designed to reflect this change.
Therefore there is a shift in emphasis away from a more linear pupil progression model based upon the teaching and generalisation of concepts, towards a model of education which recognises the pupil’s existing skills and provides carefully structured ways of further enabling them to be applied in functional, everyday contexts.
We consider this to be a move from a concept based model of education towards a context based one in which knowledge at all levels of ability will be more widely applied to everyday situations. In doing this we are aiming to utilise the final element of the student’s statutory educational entitlement, to prepare them as best we can to become active participants in, and contributors to society and achieve the highest degree of personal independence.
To externally communicate this work we provide all students with a range of tools to articulate their capability, focussing on their personal progress, personal social development and preparation for adulthood, including employment.
We help our students to achieve the highest degree of personal independence

About Frank Wise School
Frank Wise is a special school for children and young adults aged between 2 and 19. It is a school that prides itself on delivering excellence in a caring, sensitive and dynamic environment centred around the needs of the individual child. Underpinning this are our Aims and Values which can be downloaded below.
The school’s curriculum, the calibre and qualities of its staff and the school’s willingness to share with parents any aspect of their child’s education are at the heart of its success. As an outward facing school we continually seek to develop strong partnerships and are instrumental in a number of local, regional and national SEND related projects.

Accreditation
At Frank Wise School we believe that it is essential that the achievements of our pupils are celebrated as effectively as possible with as wide an audience as possible. We carefully capture a summary of each pupil’s learning against their individual targets and across the curriculum more broadly, and showcase key highlights of achievements from their year through Records of Achievement.
These include photographs and video footage distributed as an end of year summary as part of the Annual Review process. As well as highlighting individual achievements, we also celebrate whole class achievements and experiences such as involvement in school productions or going on day trips and residential visits.
Following a process of careful consultation with families and the evaluation of impact on pupil outcomes beyond the school, we took the decision to discontinue our use of commercial accreditation systems. This was on the basis that they are poorly understood and, as such, have limited currency in the wider world, risk distracting from a focus on the developmental requirements of the individual and were rarely considered by the pupils’ destinations. Instead, we work towards the pupils leaving in Year 14 with a personal portfolio of competency, aligned to their EHCP outcomes and supplemented with developmentally appropriate evidence of capability linked to their intended destinations, be that further education, employment or care settings.
Careers Education
Here you will find individual information for families, employers and staff along with a copy of the school’s careers program and the careers education and post school guidance policy. ‘The World of Work’ is part of the curriculum that is taught to all students as they move through the school. This is via classroom based learning, work place visits, work placements, development of skills for independence and visits into school by local employers. Independent advice and guidance is available for every young person and their family throughout their time at the school.
Pupils take part in a range of timely activities presented according to their individual needs. This ensures that they are well informed and able to play an active part in determining their future pathways post school. Professional Resources
As an outward facing school we are very open to sharing the resources and materials we develop as part of our work to meet the needs of the pupils at Frank Wise, but also as part of the work we do with other organisations. As such you can download the materials here for free.

Here you can find the overview of how we approach the evaluation of the effectiveness of our teaching practice. You can also download the questions that we use to support the process of evaluating what we do in the classroom.

Friends of FWS
Friends of Frank Wise School
The Friends of Frank Wise School is a charitable group with the aim of increasing the provision of specialised resources, facilities and equipment in order to support the work of Frank Wise School. We also raise awareness of the work of the school within the wider community.
Registered charity number 800362.
The aims of the Friends are:
What we do:
Membership of the Friends is open to all parents of pupils at the school, school staff and any member of the community who wishes to encourage the aims of the Friends of Frank Wise School.
Past fundraising priorities have been a tremendous success and we have recently been able to enhance the Secondary playground with outdoor fitness equipment and support the renovation of the Primary playground with new permanent equipment and all weather surfacing.
We are still aiming to replace the current fleet of aging minibuses, as well as continuing to support off site activities, trips and visits. If you wish to help with our ongoing fund-raising you can do so via our Just Giving page.
Historically, we have been responsible for the purchase of many items of equipment, as well as opportunities for our young people:
All this has only been possible because of our dedicated committee members and huge support from both business and the local community.
How you can help:
We rely on your generosity to continue our work. Please,
We are currently actively seeking new members. Call 01295 263520, email info@frankwise.oxon.sch.uk or contact us on Facebook to join us and for more information on the options above.
